**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination — Total shoulder replacement (CPT 23472)**
**Member:** Reese Carter
**Member ID:** W451155739
**Reference number:** POC-EF30A43966-84895
**Date of denial notice:** 2026-08-18
**Plan:** Iowa Total Care (Commercial/ACA), State of Iowa
**Governing policy:** 2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines — https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2026-05/2026%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines.pdf

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for a total shoulder replacement (CPT 23472), which my plan denied on 2026-08-18. The notice states that the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery. I am asking for reconsideration, because my records do document that treatment, and my surgeon, Dr. Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed.

Below I have set out the plan's own published criteria and matched each one to what is already in my chart.

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

**1. Conservative treatment**

The 2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines state:

> "Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-operative treatment that includes at least ONE of the following:"

That sentence ends in a colon and introduces a list of options. Two of those options in the policy are:

> "Physical therapy or properly instructed home exercise program"

> "Pharmacologic treatment (oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, analgesics)"

My records show both, not just one:

- **Physical therapy:** supervised physical therapy focused on range of motion and periscapular strengthening, 14 weeks, from 2026-04-12 to 2026-07-19, with 16 visits completed. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication:** NSAIDs for 6 months, with inadequate relief.

Fourteen weeks of supervised physical therapy is longer than the twelve weeks the policy requires, and it was completed before the request for surgery was submitted. I also had a corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-07, which gave only about 4 weeks of partial relief.

The policy also states:

> "*NOTE: In those with bone-on-bone articulation on axillary or true AP X-rays, non-operative treatment is not required"

My radiographs of 2026-06-04 (true AP and axillary views) show complete loss of glenohumeral joint space with osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and a flattened glenoid. So my records satisfy the conservative care requirement twice over: I completed more than twelve weeks of non-operative treatment, and my X-rays show the bone-on-bone findings for which the policy states non-operative treatment is not required.

**2. Timing criteria**

The policy states:

> "No cortisone injection into the joint within 12 weeks of surgery"

> "No prior arthroscopic surgery of the shoulder within 12 weeks of surgery"

My injection was on 2026-06-07. I have had no arthroscopic surgery of this shoulder. Surgery has not been performed, because authorization was denied. My surgery date is [scheduled surgery date, to be confirmed], and I ask that this timing criterion be applied to that date rather than treated as a reason for denial.

**3. Imaging and the extent of disease**

The policy states:

> "Complete or near-complete loss of joint space* on axillary or AP X-rays (internal rotation and/or external rotation)*"

> "NOTE: MRI should not be the primary imaging study to determine the extent of disease"

My 2026-06-04 shoulder radiographs (true AP and axillary) show complete loss of glenohumeral joint space with osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and a flattened glenoid. The extent of disease was established by X-ray, exactly as the policy directs.

**4. Rotator cuff and deltoid**

The policy states:

> "Functional and intact rotator cuff and deltoid (adequate abduction strength); confirmed by physical examination, MRI, or CT scan"

My CT confirms an intact rotator cuff, and my physical examination documents that cuff strength is intact.

**5. Arthritis with functional limitation, and correlation of symptoms with findings**

The policy states:

> "Evidence of painful osteoarthritis or inflammatory, non-infectious arthritis (e.g., rheumatoid) with functional limitations such as ADLs, employment, or recreation"

> "Individual has limited function (age-appropriate activities of active daily livings (ADLs), occupational, or athletic)"

> "Clinical correlation of individual's subjective complaints with objective exam findings and/or imaging (when applicable)"

> "Symptom onset, duration, and severity"

> "Type and duration of non-operative management modalities"

I have had 24 months of progressive shoulder pain that is not relieved by rest. I cannot reach overhead, dress without help, or sleep on the affected side. On examination I have glenohumeral crepitus, active forward elevation limited to 90 degrees, and external rotation limited to 10 degrees. My symptoms, my exam findings, and my X-ray findings all point to the same joint and the same diagnosis, and the type and duration of my non-operative care is documented above.

**6. Surgical readiness**

The policy states:

> "Individual does not have an active local or systemic infection"

> "Individual has good oral hygiene and does not have major dental work scheduled or"

> "Individual is medically stable and optimized for surgery, and any treatable comorbidities are adequately medically managed such as diabetes, nicotine addiction, or an excessively high BMI."

My records document no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker. If the plan needs a dental status confirmation, my surgeon's office can supply it on request.

## Request for the criteria that were actually applied

The excerpts I have quoted are the only policy text available to me, and at least one of them introduces a list of further conditions that is not reproduced in what I have. The plan holds the complete criteria it applied to my request. I am asking the plan to provide me, in writing and at no cost, the specific medical policy and clinical review criteria used to deny CPT 23472 for me, including the section and the exact requirement the reviewer found unmet, and the credentials of the reviewer who made the determination. I understand that Iowa Total Care may route musculoskeletal surgery requests to Evolent, whose guidelines are published on RadMD; if that is what happened here, please confirm it and identify the guideline section applied.

## What I am asking for

I ask that the plan overturn the denial dated 2026-08-18 and authorize the total shoulder replacement (CPT 23472) requested by Dr. Reyes. If the denial is upheld in whole or in part, please send me a written explanation that identifies the specific criterion not met and the records reviewed, along with information about my right to a further appeal and to external review.

The notice I received states that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by 2027-02-14, and I am submitting this letter well within that period. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter and following the instructions given in that notice. If there is a different form or address I should use, please let me know in writing.

Enclosed with this letter: [list enclosures — e.g., physical therapy discharge note, radiology report dated 2026-06-04, CT report, office notes from Dr. Reyes, copy of the denial notice].

Thank you for reviewing my appeal.

Sincerely,

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_
Reese Carter
Member ID: W451155739
Date of birth: [DOB]
[Phone] | [Email]
